summary: Ran one step: M4-S01, owned by metadata-builder. The step was returned by `build_plan.py next --milestone M4` (plain `next` stops at M3 because M3-S05 is blocked), was claimed pending -> running, and the owning agent's Plan was executed inline — this host's non-Agent-tool form. It wrote four files under artefacts/M4-S01/, three declared and one (deploy-order.md) undeclared by design, and check-outputs returned ok on all three declared outputs. The step was nonetheless set blocked with reason `checker-policy`, because the owning agent returned a REFUSAL_NEEDS_HUMAN_REVIEW envelope: the checker this step's own acceptance_tests[0] declares with expected exit 0 rejects the plan-mandated 'Severity 1 24x7' calendar, whose all-midnight seven-day shape is both the only always-open form the cited skill documents and the exact shape that checker rule exists to catch. Setting the step built would have handed the tester a step with a known-red declared test; deleting the calendar would have overruled the plan. Both envelopes validate.
confidence_rationale: Step 9 rubric, LOW row: the step was set blocked. The HIGH conditions otherwise held — the step was in `next`, every required input resolved from the plan, both envelopes validate, check-outputs exited 0 and nothing was written outside artefacts/M4-S01/.

process_observations.observation: The CLI quirk the caller flagged reproduced exactly: plain `next` stops at M3 because M3-S05 is blocked, while `next --milestone M4` returns M4-S01 as the only runnable step, and `set-status running` then accepted the claim without argument.

The owning agent is build-aware — the Step 4 grep over agents/metadata-builder/AGENT.md returned 39 build-layer mentions — so every file landed under artefacts/M4-S01/ on the first attempt and no Step 7 relocation was needed.

A step whose inputs and manual acceptance test both require an always-open calendar declares, as its own first acceptance test, a checker that rejects every always-open calendar; the test's description enumerates three of that checker's rules and not the one that fires, so plan verification had nothing to catch it on.

Blocking M4-S01 blocks the milestone: M4-S02 and M4-S04 both list it in depends_on, and M4-S03 depends on M4-S02, so three of M4's five steps wait on a decision that is one amend-step or one checker-rule change.

Neither agent's Wave 10 report pair under docs/reports/ was written, because the invocation constrained writes to the build directory; the build-scoped envelopes under envelopes/M4-S01/ are complete and both validate.

The blocked reason `checker-policy` is not one of the two slugs the runner's Step 8 names; it was coined because the cause is neither a skill gap (the skill documents every element written) nor a missing input, and Step 8 explicitly allows a short slug of its own for any other blocking cause.

The owning agent returned a refusal block (REFUSAL_NEEDS_HUMAN_REVIEW) alongside a complete deliverable rather than instead of one, which this agent's Step 8 reads as the `blocked` path ('the agent refused') rather than as a runner-level refusal that would have left the step stranded at `running`.
The decision this step is blocked on is a plan question — whether the 24/7 promise lives in a calendar or in an escalation entry — and it touches M4-S01 and M4-S04 together.
